7519ed6020.q: What was Harry Chin's career path before becoming a mixologist at Pigeonhole Honolulu?
7519ed6020.a: Harry was a middle school teacher teaching sixth, seventh, and eighth grade dance, theater, math and science after college. He worked as both a teaching assistant and substitute teacher before becoming a full-time teacher. During summers to sustain himself due to low teacher pay, he worked as a barista at a coffee shop, then discovered the craft cocktail bar trend in Los Angeles and was invited to barback at Kanye Rumbar, which was run by Daniel Crouch and Alan Katz. After a year of doing both jobs simultaneously on three to four hours of sleep per day, he made the decision to leave teaching and pursue bartending full-time.

3731e0613f.q: How does Harry Chin approach teaching bartenders and mixology at Pigeonhole Honolulu differently from traditional cocktail training?
3731e0613f.a: Harry emphasizes that good mixology is not about memorizing 100 or 200 classic cocktails, though learning fundamentals and classic cocktails is important. The core philosophy is trusting your palate and understanding what tastes too sweet or too spicy for you compared to what customers prefer, with focus on customer service and figuring out what individual guests want. At Pigeonhole, he prefers hiring less experienced bartenders to teach them the right way from the ground up without bad habits, using an educational mentality as the core of the bar program.

461104b2c4.q: What local Hawaiian ingredients does Harry Chin use in cocktails at Pigeonhole Honolulu?
461104b2c4.a: Harry uses abundant tropical fruits including fresh pineapples, passion fruit, and lilikoi, emphasizing that fresh ingredients make all the difference compared to canned alternatives used by tourist establishments. He also leverages pandan, which is gaining popularity globally. One unique local ingredient is pickled orchids—edible purple orchids used as garnish in Hawaiian dishes—which he pickles and incorporates into drinks like the Queen's Pog Swizzle for peppery floral flavors and acid.

ff621eee9d.q: Why did Harry Chin move from Los Angeles to Honolulu and how did it influence his cocktail philosophy?
ff621eee9d.a: Harry's move was unexpected—he came to Honolulu during COVID to visit his brother, and a one to two month visit turned into a job offer and a three-year position as a cook at a restaurant. He decided to stay permanently. While he doesn't see major flavor preference differences between Los Angeles and Hawaii aside from tropical fruit abundance, he embraces the tropical drink style but insists on using fresh pineapples and local ingredients rather than canned alternatives, arguing that if bars take tropical drinks seriously they should utilize the freshest ingredients available.

4384418e07.q: What is the Queen's Pog Swizzle at Pigeonhole Honolulu and what ingredients does it contain?
4384418e07.a: The Queen's Pog Swizzle is a local play on the classic Queen's Park Swizzle and an ode to Queen Kapiolani. It is a mojito variation without soda water, made with mint, fresh lilikoi or passion fruit with seeds, pickled orchids for acid and floral peppery notes, and local rum from Kuleana. The drink showcases Harry's approach to using fresh local Hawaiian ingredients and turning edible orchids into cocktail components.

a0fb4022ef.q: What dish at Kapa Hale best represents Chef Keaka Lee's cooking philosophy?
a0fb4022ef.a: Chef Lee would choose the chicken dish, sourced from Ludovico Farm in North Shore, which uses Korean raising practices. He seasons it with a homemade kalamansi kosho—a citrus pepper made from kalamansi limes, salt, and Hawaiian chilies—based on techniques from Jonathan Waxman's roasted chicken at Bacchanal in New York. The dish is brined, spatchcocked, finished on the grill for smoky flavor and charred skin, then paired with potatoes and calamansi salsa verde. He emphasizes that the chicken itself holds the dish together, not the sauce.

5648b6470b.q: How does Chef Keaka Lee incorporate soy sauce into dessert at Kapa Hale?
5648b6470b.a: Lee created a maple soy sauce crème brûlée, paired with kaki mochi (Hawaiian mochi snack also called bubu arare in Japanese). The inspiration came five years ago when an event asked him to pair something with natto; he experimented with soy sauce in a pineapple upside-down cake where caramelization of both the cake and pineapple complemented the soy. He uses soy sauce in minimal amounts to find the right balance, as the ingredient is unexpected in desserts.

c67848d592.q: What changes did Chef Keaka Lee make to his Hawaiian Airlines menu after the 2024 first-class launch?
c67848d592.a: Lee has worked with Hawaiian Airlines since 2022, with the first-class menu debuting in 2024. After Alaska Airlines acquired Hawaiian Airlines, the expansion allowed more Hawaiian ingredients on menus. For 2026, he featured ulu (breadfruit) on the planes. Key lesson: at 10,000 feet altitude, passengers lose taste buds, requiring higher salt levels in dishes. Lee learned to keep recipes simple and account for the science of meal heating, container placement, and food stability over four-hour flight durations.

c5d11b9dd2.q: How did opening Kapa Hale during the COVID-19 pandemic influence Chef Keaka Lee's priorities as a restaurant owner?
c5d11b9dd2.a: Lee signed the lease in November 2019, and his daughter Astoria was born in January 2020, just before the pandemic hit in February-March. Despite initial anxiety about protecting his family, he approached the challenge by drafting a lease agreement allowing closure before opening to avoid financial ruin. Becoming a father shifted his definition of success: he now prioritizes being a great father, husband, and family man before being a great chef, sometimes taking two hours away from the business to pick up his daughter from school or attend her soccer games.

01b56f16b4.q: What did Mike Anthony teach Chef Keaka Lee about managing younger generation cooks?
01b56f16b4.a: Lee initially held the attitude that younger cooks were soft compared to his generation, which had endured pots and pans being thrown and burns. Mike Anthony, his former chef at Gramercy Tavern and at Untitled and Studio Cafe in New York, pulled him aside and challenged this mindset, explaining that Lee's dismissive attitude toward younger workers was counterproductive. This conversation changed Lee's approach to building his kitchen culture and respecting the next generation.
